principles.title: Privacy is baseline
principles.definition: Not a feature. Not optional. Encryption is how open societies work.

principles.title: We are sovereign nodes
principles.definition: You own your agency. Wallet, device, person, service. The power to choose. The power to leave. The power to fork.

principles.title: No choke points
principles.definition: AWS. Google. Azure. Cloudflare. ICANN. Any can flick a switch. We won't build castles on their infrastructure.

principles.title: We are Cypherpunks
principles.definition: We write code. We publish it. We build systems that can't be shut down.

principles.title: Web3 is for users, not builders
principles.definition: Not your product. Not your attention. Not your data. You are the point.

principles.title: We reject capture
principles.definition: VC rent-seeking. DINO projects. EEE tactics. We build tools, not toll booths.

principles.title: Access is a right
principles.definition: The last mile is the hardest mile. We build for real users.

principles.title: Bitcoin doesn't care
principles.definition: It just works. Don't worship money. Use it.

principles.title: IP enforcement is ending
principles.definition: Open P2P makes it impossible. Patronage replaces licensing.

principles.title: Resilience over perfection
principles.definition: Build for failure. Fragility teaches. Emergent harmony beats chaos and control.

principles.title: Anti-idolatry
principles.definition: Don't worship these words. Fork them. Challenge them.

story.title: THE INHERITANCE
story.content:
Eric Hughes wrote: "Privacy is necessary for an open society." He warned us we couldn't expect governments or corporations to grant us privacy. We had to defend it ourselves. Cypherpunks write code.

Information doesn't just want to be free. It longs to be free.

What he called "anonymous transaction systems" is now blockchains. The technology caught up. The ethos didn't.

We didn't listen. By the mid-2000s, platforms grew. By the 2010s, they dominated. Users became products.

story.title: THE RESONANCE
story.summary: We weren't alone in thinking this
story.content:
Later, work we found articulated what we felt:

"Sovereignty is no longer an abstract ideal but a practice - a discipline born of code."

"Autonomy is not isolation. It is interdependence without subservience."

"The power to walk away. The power to fork. The power to choose a different path."

We weren't alone.

story.title: THE NOW
story.summary: Thirty years of evidence. Time to build.
story.content:
We've watched Big Tech consolidate. AWS. Google. Azure. Cloudflare. ICANN. Any can flick a switch.

We've watched web3 become a casino. Money over freedom. Scams over solutions.

We've watched VC capture. For-profit focus turned public infrastructure into extractive platforms.

We're not here to repeat warnings. We're here to build.

These manifestos informed our thinking:
• A Cypherpunk's Manifesto (1993) - Eric Hughes
• The Autonomist Manifesto (2025)

problems.title: INFRASTRUCTURE CAPTURE
problems.summary: Three companies can flick the switch
problems.content:
AWS. Google. Azure. Cloudflare. ICANN.

Any of them can flick a switch tomorrow. Most of what we call "web3" would disappear.

We're not ready.

problems.title: VC EXTRACTION
problems.content:
Venture capital funded R&D. That's valuable.

But extraction overshadowed the good. For-profit focus turned web3 into a new walled garden.

Public infrastructure cannot be funded with extractive capital.

problems.title: DINO PROJECTS
problems.content:
Red flags:

- Claims decentralization, runs on AWS
- VC-owned, calls itself community
- Token sold as ownership - it's not
- Closed-source "trust me bro"
- Business licenses in DeFi

problems.title: THE CASINO
problems.content:
DeFi became gambling. NFTs became speculation.

"Just trust me bro" replaced trustlessness.

problems.title: THE ACCESS GAP
problems.content:
Infrastructure exists. The access layer is broken.

The last mile is the hardest mile.

And frankly, it's a joke.

path.title: WHAT WE BUILD
path.content:
We publish code. We build systems that can't be shut down.

Infrastructure that doesn't depend on Big Tech. Access layers that work for real users. Protocols that resist capture.

path.title: HOW WE FUND
path.content:
Not extraction. Not rent-seeking. Not VC returns.

If we can't sustain without exploiting users, we're doing it wrong.

path.title: SUCCESS METRICS
path.summary: If web3 is invisible, it worked
path.content:
If you use web3 and don't notice it's different from web2 - if it's boring, if it just works - only then we succeeded.

The standard, not the exception.
